ONE KNOB: recon_eta 30.0->1.0 (DPS guidance gain). iter-1 (eta=30) = SSIM 0.3937 / hr 0.0 / PSNR 14.31 / RMSE 0.00963 — FAR BELOW the ~0.81 LD-FBP floor, i.e. the recon is corrupted relative to its own FBP init, not merely prior-dominated drift. Failure mode: the DPS step is adaptively normalized in-solver (step = (eta/||resid||)*grad, Chung 2023 eq.12), so eta is a dimensionless gain whose literature/demo/breast default is 1.0; eta=30 (a discarded-614 boundary-metric hint) is a 30x overshoot that, with recon_eta_clamp=false (no per-step displacement cap), blows the FBP-initialized iterate off-manifold every reverse step, and the relax=1.0 hard-DC then re-noises a corrupted x0. HYPOTHESIS: lowering eta 30->1 lets the DPS correction be a gentle pull, recovering SSIM from 0.39 toward/above the ~0.81 LD-FBP floor (hr>0). FALSIFIER: if SSIM stays ~0.39-0.5 (still <<FBP) at eta=1, the DPS step size was NOT the issue — the Mayo v4 DDPM prior is mismatched to rebinned Mayo under the 25-step low-T budget (mirrors the breast-DDPM hr=0 structural verdict: globally faithful but not conditionally faithful under DPS/DC) -> iter-3 redirects to the prior, not the DC weight. BUDGET: eta is free (no per-slice cost change); iter-1 ran 214 slices in 1018.96 s = 4.76 s/slice = 17.0 min < 20-min wall (1800s in-solver backstop never hit). val=ALL 214 L277, 321px geometry FOV default.

TRAJECTORY: iter-1 eta=30 SSIM 0.3937/hr0; iter-2 eta 30->1 REGRESSED to SSIM 0.2366/hr0 -> eta is the WRONG lever (gentling the DPS gain did not help; the corruption is elsewhere). FAILURE MODE (numbers): both prior iters ran recon_dcstep_relax=1.0 = FULL hard projection. In dc_step_cg() the return is relax*x_cg + (1-relax)*x0_mu; relax=1.0 discards the diffusion x0 estimate ENTIRELY and substitutes n_cg=3 Gauss-Newton least-squares fit to the NOISY 2304-view LD sinogram, which is then re-noised back to t_next every 5 reverse steps (warmup 5). That least-squares fit overfits measurement noise and overwrites the prior's structure -> hard-CG DC re-noises a corrupted x0, exactly the constrained variant's failure. The SOLVER DEFAULT is relax=0.5; relax=1.0 was an untested aggressive choice carried from iter-1. ONE KNOB: relax 1.0->0.3 blends 30% CG-projected + 70% diffusion x0, a GENTLE pull to data consistency that preserves prior structure instead of overwriting it. HYPOTHESIS: softening the hard-DC blend lifts SSIM back toward / above the ~0.81 LD-FBP floor (hr>0); predicted iter-3 SSIM 0.4-0.7 range (recovery from 0.2366). FALSIFIER: if SSIM stays well below FBP (~0.3 vs 0.81) even at relax=0.3, the Mayo v4 DDPM prior is STRUCTURALLY MISMATCHED to rebinned Mayo under the 25-step low-T DPS/DC budget (mirrors the breast-DDPM hr=0 verdict: globally faithful but not conditionally faithful) -> NEGATIVE RESULT, STOP diffusion on Mayo. BUDGET: relax is a blend scalar inside dc_step_cg -> ZERO compute change (same n_cg=3, n_steps=25, DC cadence every5). iter-2 ran ALL 214 L277 slices in 1033.8 s = 4.83 s/slice = 17.2 min < 20-min wall (1800s in-solver backstop never hit); iter-1 1018.96 s. iter-3 lands ~17 min, inside budget. val=ALL 214 L277, 321px detector-geometry FOV default.

ONE KNOB: recon_dc_solver legacy->cg (NEW config-gated correct DC path in solver_diffusion_recon.py; legacy path byte-for-byte preserved + reproducible for all prior cfgs). The audit found the legacy DC-step is (1) a MISLABELED steepest-descent dressed as CG (dc_step_cg lines ~83-100) and (2) a re-injection that recomputes x0 from a STALE eps via x0_from_eps(x,eps,ab_next) then re-noises with a FRESH randn mid-schedule (lines ~162-174) — this collapsed unconstrained iter-4 to SSIM 0.055 and kept the constrained variant stuck 0.24-0.66 << the ~0.81 LD-FBP floor at hr=0. THE FIX (ported from the corrected solver_fast_recon.cg_data_consistency): recon_dc_solver=cg swaps in a GENUINE Fletcher-Reeves CG solve of AtA x = At y (residual + conjugate direction + FR beta), forms x0 from the CURRENT step's eps (x0_hat at t_now, not a stale eps re-eval'd at the wrong alpha_bar), CG-projects it, then re-embeds at t_next DETERMINISTICALLY as sqrt(ab_next)*x0_proj_norm + sqrt(1-ab_next)*eps_pred reusing the SAME eps (eps-prediction => the level-t noise direction IS eps_pred) — NO fresh randn, NO stale eps. BASE = iter-5 BEST (T=40, eta=30, relax=1.0, every5/n_cg3/warmup5, val_n=120, SSIM 0.6647/hr0 — the run-best constrained config). Hard DC stays ON (recon_dcstep_every=5) now that it is CORRECT. HONEST EXPECTATION: the corrected CG-DC should STOP the legacy re-noise corruption and likely RAISE SSIM above iter-5's 0.6647 (the deterministic same-eps re-embed no longer overwrites the trajectory with fresh noise + a least-squares fit to the noisy 2304-view LD sinogram). But on DENSE rebinned Mayo (LD-FBP near-complete at 2304 views) the v4 DDPM prior is regime-bounded, so hr may STILL be ~0 — the real payoff is the 128-view SPARSE benchmarks + the planned EMA v5 prior. This iter VALIDATES the fix RUNS and is NON-REGRESSIVE/non-corrupting under the corrected metric. FALSIFIER: if SSIM drops below iter-5's 0.6647 the corrected re-embed is mis-scaling x0 vs eps; if it clears the ~0.81 FBP floor (hr>0) the legacy bug was the whole story. BUDGET: recon_dc_solver=cg is roughly cost-neutral vs legacy (the DPS forward+grad per step is unchanged; the CG inner loop does forward+back per n_cg, comparable to legacy dc_step_cg's forward+back+forward; the deterministic re-embed drops the randn). iter-5 ran T=40 x val_n=120 in 988.0 s = 16.5 min < the HARD 1200s/20-min budget (1800s in-solver backstop + 30-min --time). val_n=120 held at iter-5's value (no reduction needed — 988s leaves ~3.5 min headroom for the CG path's marginal delta). val=120 evenly-spaced L277, 321px detector-geometry FOV default (no fov=False). staged_canonical data, v3 mayo_ldct_fitted geometry, per-sample-ps single-val-ps probe, bg_target=truth, reuse ddpm_mayo_constrained_v4.pt (NO retrain), 321px FOV.
